pairs.question: Chreme, tantumne ab re tuast oti tibi aliena ut cures ea quae nil ad te attinent?
pairs.answer: Homo sum: humani nil a me alienum puto.
pairs.derivation: Menedemus asks Chremes why he has so much leisure from his own affairs as to mind business that does not concern him; Chremes answers with the famous line. Answer ends at the first full stop, before he continues 'vel me monere hoc vel percontari puta...'. No framing to drop.

pairs.question: An quoiquamst usus homini se ut cruciet?
pairs.derivation: Chremes asks whether it is of any use to a man to torment himself; Menedemus answers 'mihi' (to me [it is]), a genuine reply to the question. Self-contained general question.

pairs.question: Num quid nam de gnato meo audisti, Chreme?
pairs.derivation: Menedemus asks whether Chremes has heard anything about his son; Chremes answers that he is well and alive. Clean polar question genuinely answered.

pairs.question: Non tu illi dixti ut essem? Non. Quam ob rem, Chreme?
pairs.answer: Quia pessume istuc in te atque illum consulis, si te tam leni et victo esse animo ostenderis.
pairs.derivation: Setup kept verbatim: Menedemus asks 'didn't you tell him I'd be [home]?' (answered 'non' by Chremes) so that the operative 'quam ob rem' has its referent; the why-question is then answered by Chremes with 'quia...'. Editorial bracket '[in]' before 'illum' dropped, keeping no extra words (the bracketed 'in' is a deletion, not a supplement — the running text reads 'atque illum'). Answer ends at the full stop before the next speaker.

pairs.question: Quid nunc facere cogitas?
pairs.answer: Ad Menedemum ibo: dicam hanc esse captam ex Caria ditem et nobilem; si redimat magnum inesse in ea lucrum.
pairs.derivation: Chremes asks Syrus what he now plans to do. Syrus's reply opens with the non-answering counter-question 'egon?' ('Me?'), so the answer-start is advanced past it to the operative answering sentence 'ad Menedemum ibo...'. Span runs to the end of Syrus's plan; the following line is Chremes's objection 'erras'.

pairs.question: Immo filium iube potiu'. Quam ob rem?
pairs.answer: Quia enim in eum suspiciost translata amori'.
pairs.derivation: Syrus's setup 'immo filium iube potiu'' is kept verbatim so Chremes's 'quam ob rem?' ('why?') has its referent; Syrus answers with 'quia enim in eum suspiciost translata amoris' (because suspicion of the love affair has been shifted onto him). Answer ends at the full stop before the next exchange 'quid tum?'.
